newsitem.title: INDIA: India shares end with small losses in dull trade.
newsitem.headline: India shares end with small losses in dull trade.

text.p: Indian stocks suffered minor losses on Thursday in a session that largely lacked direction, said traders.
The Bombay Stock Exchange's (BSE) 30-share index ended 34.24 points, or 0.97 points down at 3,494.20.
The local market was unaffected by news of the overnight death of Chinese leader Deng Xiaoping, dealers said.

"The market was very sluggish. Institutional participation is not coming in," said Govind Agarwal, dealer at institutional brokerge Motilal Oswal. "Speculators who had built up positions hoping that funds would start buying are now squaring up."

India's main opposition party on Thursday backtracked on a bid to topple Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda, saying it would not press for a no-confidence vote against the government it had earlier planned for Friday.

"We are not interested in a no-confidence motion early in the budget session," former prime minister Atal Behari Vajpayee, the leader of the Bharatiya Janata Party, told Reuters. "We want it as the last weapon." The 1997 budget is on February 28.
But dealers said the news failed to enthuse sentiments as an absence of buying support continued to pull down prices. "Poor volumes were a casualty in a dull market," one dealer said.
The BSE said on Thursday shares of state-run Bank of Baroda would be listed on February 21.
Bank of Baroda launched its 8.5 billion rupee initial public offer last December. The bank had offered 100 million shares of 10 rupees face value at 85 rupees a share.
Shares of cement-maker ACC shed 40.0 rupees to 1,439.0 in volatile trade. "The stock is in the grip of speculators who are dictating prices," said a local dealer.
SBI fell 3.50 rupees to 285.75 and TISCO 3.0 to 190.75.
